ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The diagram shows a convex quadrilateral ABCD with side labels AB=3, BC=4, CD=12, DA=13, and a right-angle mark at B between BA and BC. Reasoning: Draw diagonal AC, which splits the convex quadrilateral into triangles ABC and ACD. Since angle CBA is right and AB=3, BC=4, triangle ABC is a 3-4-5 right triangle, so AC=sqrt(3^2+4^2)=5. Its area is (1/2)(3)(4)=6. Triangle ACD then has side lengths AC=5, CD=12, and DA=13. Since 5^2+12^2=13^2, triangle ACD is right, so its area is (1/2)(5)(12)=30. Adding the two triangle areas gives 6+30=36.
